q: Why does a command use a cloud call?
a: Atomberg allows 100 calls a day. A fan that is heard on your Wi‑Fi is controlled directly and costs none. Otherwise a command is one call.

q: Why isn’t my fan found locally?
a: The fan and this Mac must be on the same Wi‑Fi, and Local Network access must be on for this app. Tap the wifi button to look again.

q: What do Local and Cloud mean?
a: Local: the command goes over your Wi‑Fi. Cloud: it goes through Atomberg’s servers and counts toward the daily limit.
In your macOS Keychain, nowhere else. They are sent only to Atomberg’s API.
api.developer.atomberg-iot.com over HTTPS, and your fans on UDP ports 5625 and 5600. Nothing else. No analytics, no updater.

q: Why does the Keychain ask for access?
a: macOS asks when it does not recognise the app. Choose Always Allow once.
Settings → Replace Credentials. To remove everything, delete the app and the Keychain item “com.ashwin.ATOMBERG”.
No. It is unofficial and not affiliated with Atomberg. Source-available under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.

q: Which Atomberg devices does it support?
a: Whatever your developer account lists: fans (local network and cloud), water purifiers and smart locks (cloud only). Local control over UDP exists for fans only.
Yes, for noncommercial use. It is source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, so commercial use is not allowed.

q: What do I need to run it?
a: macOS 26 or later, and an Atomberg account with Developer Mode turned on in the Atomberg Home app to get an API key and refresh token.

Quit it from the power button, delete Atomberg Console.app, then remove ~/Library/Application Support/ATOMBERG and the Keychain item “com.ashwin.ATOMBERG”. With Homebrew: brew uninstall --zap --cask atomberg-console.
